summary.headline: Rushil Decor Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 25.3% YoY to Rs 2,953 mn, a record, with PAT up 96.6% to Rs 101 mn.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue for both the laminate and MDF segments in Q2 FY27, with consolidated EBITDA up 24.5% YoY to Rs 280 mn at a 9.5% margin. Jumbo Laminates scaled up sharply, with revenue up 97.3% QoQ to Rs 217 mn and a 19.4% EBITDA margin, while MDF capacity utilisation rose to 87% from 66% in Q1 with no exports. Management said blended laminate margins are under pressure from raw material and freight costs, with a laminate price hike taken after 10 October 2026. Capex guidance is limited to Rs 15-20 crore from internal accruals, and management has not yet decided on any fresh expansion.

segments.name: MDF
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue Rs 1,962 mn (+15.8% YoY, record) with EBITDA Rs 194 mn (+6% YoY, margin about 9.9%); India MDF revenue +41% YoY and no exports in the quarter. H1 revenue Rs 3,418 mn (+16.4%), EBITDA Rs 317 mn at 9.3% margin vs 3.7% in H1 FY26.

segments.name: Laminates (total)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue Rs 884 mn (+61.7% YoY, record), with India Rs 404 mn (+82.1%) and exports Rs 480 mn (+47.7%); volume about 10.4 lakh sheets (+32.8%); blended realisation Rs 847/sheet (+21.7%). EBITDA Rs 85 mn (margin 9.6% vs 7.7%). H1 revenue Rs 1,622 mn (+63.3%), EBITDA Rs 137 mn (8.4% margin).

segments.name: Jumbo Laminates
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue Rs 217 mn (+97.3% QoQ), volumes more than tripled QoQ; EBITDA Rs 42 mn (vs Rs 23 mn in Q1), margin 19.4%. Capacity utilisation 41%.

segments.name: PVC
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue Rs 103 mn (+14.3% YoY), volume +11.8%, realisation +2.3%; EBITDA Rs 2 mn (2.4% margin). H1 revenue Rs 200 mn (+13.7%), EBITDA Rs 10 mn (5.1% margin).

guidance_outlook: FY27 full-year performance expected to be better than H1; no quantified revenue or EBITDA guidance given, and no FY28 guidance.
Management commits to a 12-14% EBITDA margin for the laminate business as a whole once utilisation rises; current blended laminate margin is about 10% (about 12% including Jumbo).
MDF capacity utilisation expected at 82-85% across FY27; targets of 50% of MDF volume and 60% of MDF revenue from value-added products during FY27 (H1: 44% and 55%).
Jumbo Laminates utilisation targeted at 80-85% by March 2027 (from 41%); management indicated Rs 80-100 crore annual Jumbo revenue is possible at that level.
Capex for FY27 limited to normal operational capex of about Rs 15-20 crore from internal accruals (about Rs 14 crore spent in H1).
Laminate price hike taken after 10 October 2026, which should flow into Q3.
capex_capacity: MDF capacity utilisation 87% in Q2 FY27 vs 66% in Q1; management expects 82-85% utilisation through FY27.
Jumbo Laminates utilisation 41% in Q2 FY27; target 80-85% by March 2027.

Management is reviewing a possible fresh capex for MDF or Jumbo Laminates for FY28-FY29; no decision yet, with an announcement possible around end of Q3 FY27. Brownfield lead time for the main machine is about 8 months.
Management hopes laminate becomes at least equal in size to MDF within a couple of years.
demand_pricing: MDF domestic realisation fell about 7% QoQ, attributed to raw material volatility, price pressure and 5-10% competition; management said domestic competition will keep pressure on pricing for one more quarter.

Export of MDF paused amid western-world tensions and high freight (ocean freight cited at about USD 8,000 vs USD 800-900 earlier); strategy is calibrated, with a return to exports once freight normalises.
BIS certification on imports and high freight are cited as reducing MDF import threat; China not seen as a major threat, with Malaysia, Vietnam, Thailand and Indonesia cited as past threats.

Jumbo Laminates is mostly contract-based, with orders signed for Q3 and Q4 FY27; exports to 63 countries (up from 52-54), focus on Europe, Russia and Southeast Asia; Jumbo shipments largely FOB vs CIF for regular laminates.
Distribution expansion in Q2: 8 new direct distributors and 27 dealers added; OEM share about 40% of capacity utilisation, trade and retail about 60%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did MDF realisation fall QoQ and YoY despite value-added mix and a 15% price hike?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited H1 realisation of about Rs 26,600/tonne-equivalent and said YoY improvement reflects the prior-year fire at the Andhra Pradesh plant; the QoQ fall was due to volatile chemical prices, price pressure and 5-10% competition.

qa_highlights.question: What is the full-year capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said no specific additional capex beyond normal operational capex, about Rs 15-20 crore in total from internal accruals; about Rs 14 crore already spent in H1.

qa_highlights.question: Can Jumbo Laminates reach Rs 80-100 crore revenue at full utilisation with 20%+ margins?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said at 80-85% utilisation it can be Rs 80 crore or Rs 100 crore-plus depending on product mix. CEO said laminate margins will move to 12-14% as utilisation rises; freight costs are a current drag.

qa_highlights.question: Why has non-Jumbo laminate margin fallen to about 6-7%?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher raw material prices and a price hike only taken after 10 October 2026 (in Q3). Management called the current cost environment a new normal and said laminate as a whole is at 10% margin (12% including Jumbo).

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan for fresh capex in FY28-FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is still reviewing options, including greenfield or brownfield, and will announce something around the end of the quarter once utilisation data is in.

qa_highlights.question: Is any FY27 revenue or EBITDA guidance available?
qa_highlights.answer: No quantified guidance. Management said FY27 will be better than H1, and declined FY28 guidance.

risks_watch: Raw material and freight cost volatility (chemicals and ocean freight) compressing laminate and MDF margins.
MDF pricing pressure from domestic competition; realisation fell about 7% QoQ in Q2.
Dependence on domestic MDF with no exports; export restart depends on freight normalisation.
Jumbo Laminates utilisation ramp from 41% to 80-85% by March 2027; contract visibility for Q3-Q4 only.
Net debt rising to Rs 2,715 mn; payables days fell from 189 to 157, which could pressure working capital.
Pending capex decision for FY28-FY29 that could raise leverage.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line momentum and Jumbo Laminates, but cautious and often non-specific on margins, pricing, capex and FY28, deferring those to a later announcement.
key_quotes: Rushil Decor achieved its highest ever quarterly revenue during the Q2 FY27, reflecting improved business performance across our businesses.
The margin as a whole business would be 12% to 14%. And we will make sure that we achieve those numbers what we are committing of 12% to 14% margin for the laminate business as a whole.
Amount can be in the range of Rs. 15 crores to Rs. 20 crores in max which will be from internal accruals only.
I would not like to give any guidance for FY28 as of now, but so far as current financial year is concerned, it will be definitely better than H1, that is for sure.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 to be better than H1 with no quantified revenue figure, backed partly by Jumbo Laminates contract orders for Q3-Q4, a Jumbo utilisation ramp from 41% to 80-85% by March 2027, a laminate price hike after 10 Oct 2026, and MDF utilisation of 82-85%; no new capacity is being added and fresh capex is still under review.
